pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔢 **Strand 1 — Number**
Counting, calculating and reasoning with numbers — the language of trade, science and everyday life.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.1.3)
- B7.1.3.1 — Simplify, compare and order a mixture of positive fractions (common, percent and decimal) by changing all to equivalent fractions, decimals or percentages. B7.1.3.2 — Demonstrate an understanding of the process of addition and/or subtraction of fractions and apply this in solving problems. B7.1.3.3 — Demonstrate an understanding of the process of multiplying and dividing positive fractions and apply this in solving problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- recall the decimal and percentage equivalents of benchmark fractions
- simplify, compare and order common fractions, decimals and percentages
- add and subtract unlike and mixed fractions and solve problems
- multiply fractions, decimals and percentages by whole numbers and by fractions
- find a fraction of a quantity
- divide whole numbers and fractions by fractions and solve problems

pages.title: Key words and map
pages.body:
> ✨ **Key words**
- numerator
- denominator
- equivalent fraction
- simplest form
- mixed number
- improper fraction
- benchmark fraction
- reciprocal
- percentage

> 🗺️ **Sections in this chapter**
- 3.1 Reviewing fractions
- 3.2 Comparing and ordering fractions, decimals and percentages
- 3.3 Adding and subtracting fractions
- 3.4 Multiplying fractions
- 3.5 Dividing fractions

pages.title: Reviewing fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Determine and recall the percentages and decimals of given benchmark fractions (tenths, fifths, fourths, thirds and halves) and use these to compare quantities.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.3.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Fraction** — A fraction [[a/b]] names a equal parts out of b equal parts of a whole. a is the **numerator** and b (never 0) is the **denominator**.
[[fig:m7-f08|Figure 3.1: 5/6 of the rectangle is shaded]]
## Equivalent fractions and simplest form
Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number gives an **equivalent fraction**. A fraction is in its **simplest form** when the only common factor of numerator and denominator is 1.
## ✏️ Example 3.1
a) Write down three fractions equivalent to [[2/3]]. b) Express [[6/10]] in its simplest form.
**Solution**
a) [[2/3]] = [[2×2/3×2]] = [[4/6]]; [[2/3]] = [[6/9]]; [[2/3]] = [[8/12]]
b) The HCF of 6 and 10 is 2, so [[6/10]] = [[6÷2/10÷2]] = [[3/5]]
## Mixed numbers and improper fractions
## ✏️ Example 3.2
a) Convert [[29/6]] to a mixed number. b) Convert 3[[4/7]] to an improper fraction.
**Solution**
a) 29 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 5, so [[29/6]] = 4[[5/6]]
b) 3[[4/7]] = [[3×7+4/7]] = [[25/7]]
## Benchmark fractions, decimals and percentages

pages.title: Example 3.3
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 3.3
Copy and complete the table by finding the values A to L.
| **Common fraction** | [[1/10]] | [[1/5]] | [[1/4]] | [[1/3]] | [[2/5]] | [[1/2]] | [[2/3]] | [[3/4]] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Percent | 10% | 20% | D | E | 40% | 50% | F | G |
| Decimal | 0.1 | H | I | J | 0.4 | K | L | 0.75 |
**Solution**
To change a fraction to a percentage, multiply by 100%. To change it to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator.
| **Letter** | **D** | **E** | **F** | **G** | **H** | **I** | **J** | **K** | **L** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value | 25% | 33[[1/3]]% | 66[[2/3]]% | 75% | 0.2 | 0.25 | 0.333… | 0.5 | 0.666… |
**Closer to 0, closer to** [[1/2]] **or closer to 1?**
A fraction is **close to 0** when the numerator is very small compared with the denominator (e.g. [[1/9]]), **close to** [[1/2]] when the numerator is about half the denominator (e.g. [[5/11]]), and **close to 1** when the numerator is almost equal to the denominator (e.g. [[11/12]]).
[[fig:m7-f09|Figure 3.2: Benchmark fractions on a number line]]
> 🧪 **Activity 3.1 — The fraction wheel game**
1. Make a spinner divided into 8 sectors, each labelled with a fraction, e.g. [[1/8]], [[3/7]], [[9/10]], [[2/9]], [[5/9]], [[7/8]], [[1/12]], [[6/11]].
2. Make three cards labelled closer to 0, closer to [[1/2]] and closer to 1.
3. A player spins the wheel and must pick the correct card for the fraction shown. A correct answer wins a fraction card. (Cards that have been picked are not replaced.)
4. The player with the most fraction cards at the end wins.

pages.title: Simplifying and comparing fractions
pages.body:
[[fig:m7-f10|Figure 3.3: A fraction wheel]]
## Simplifying and comparing fractions
## ✏️ Example 3.4
a) Which of [[4/10]], [[4/12]], [[7/8]], [[1/3]] and [[1/4]] is the simplest form of the fraction shaded in the diagram? b) Which symbol (<, = or >) makes "[[3/5]] … [[2/3]]" true? c) Which is greater: [[7/12]] or [[8/10]]?
[[fig:m7-f11]]
**Solution**
a) 4 of the 12 equal parts are shaded: [[4/12]] = [[4÷4/12÷4]] = [[1/3]].
b) Use a common denominator 15: [[3/5]] = [[9/15]] and [[2/3]] = [[10/15]]. Since 9 < 10, [[3/5]] **<** [[2/3]].
c) LCM of 12 and 10 is 60: [[7/12]] = [[35/60]] and [[8/10]] = [[48/60]], so [[8/10]] **is greater**.

pages.title: Comparing and ordering fractions, decimals and percentages
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Compare and order fractions (common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths), limited to benchmark fractions.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.3.1.2
To compare numbers written in different forms, first change them all into the **same form** — all decimals, all percentages, or all fractions with a common denominator.
## ✏️ Example 3.5
Arrange [[5/6]], [[3/4]] and [[7/8]] in descending order.
**Solution**
LCM of 6, 4 and 8 is 24: [[5/6]] = [[20/24]], [[3/4]] = [[18/24]], [[7/8]] = [[21/24]].
Descending order: [[7/8]]**,** [[5/6]]**,** [[3/4]]
## ✏️ Example 3.6
a) Which is greater, 0.99 or 0.977? b) Order 0.098, 0.985 and 0.123 from least to greatest.
**Solution**
a) Write both with three decimal places: 0.990 and 0.977. Compare tenths: 9 = 9; hundredths: 9 > 7. So **0.99 > 0.977**.
b) Tenths digits: 0, 9, 1. So **0.098 < 0.123 < 0.985**.
## ✏️ Example 3.7
Order 0.832, [[3/8]] and 38% from least to greatest.
**Solution**
Change each to a percentage:
0.832 = [[832/1000]] = 83.2%
[[3/8]] = [[375/1000]] = 0.375 = 37.5%
38% = [[38/100]] = 0.38
Least to greatest: [[3/8]]**, 38%, 0.832**
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** 38% = 0.38, not 0.38%. When you change a percentage to a decimal, divide by 100 and drop the % sign.

pages.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Explain the process of addition and subtraction of two or three unlike and mixed fractions.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.3.2.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Adding and subtracting unlike fractions** — Change the fractions to equivalent fractions with a **common denominator** (best: the LCM of the denominators). Then add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. Simplify the answer.
[[fig:m7-f12|Figure 3.4: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6]]
## ✏️ Example 3.8
Find 2[[2/5]] + 1[[2/3]].
**Solution**
Add the whole numbers first, then the fractions (LCM of 5 and 3 is 15):
2[[2/5]] + 1[[2/3]] = (2 + 1) + [[2/5]] + [[2/3]] = 3 + [[6/15]] + [[10/15]]
= 3 + [[16/15]] = 3 + 1[[1/15]] = 4[[1/15]]
## ✏️ Example 3.9
Find 2[[4/5]] − 1[[2/3]].
**Solution**
Method 1 — whole numbers and fractions separately:
(2 − 1) + [[4/5]] − [[2/3]] = 1 + [[12 − 10/15]] = 1[[2/15]]
Method 2 — change to improper fractions:
[[14/5]] − [[5/3]] = [[42/15]] − [[25/15]] = [[17/15]] = 1[[2/15]]
## ✏️ Example 3.10
Simplify 3[[1/4]] − 1[[5/6]] + [[2/3]].
**Solution**
LCM of 4, 6 and 3 is 12.
3[[1/4]] − 1[[5/6]] + [[2/3]] = [[39/12]] − [[22/12]] + [[8/12]] = [[25/12]] = 2[[1/12]]
**Indicator B7.1.3.2.2** Solve problems involving addition or subtraction of fractions.
## ✏️ Example 3.11
3[[1/3]] feet are cut off a board that is 12[[1/4]] feet long. How long is the remaining part?
**Solution**
12[[1/4]] − 3[[1/3]] = [[49/4]] − [[10/3]] = [[147/12]] − [[40/12]] = [[107/12]] = 8[[11/12]] **feet**

pages.title: Example 3.12
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 3.12
The Musa family hiked to a waterfall about 8[[5/8]] km away. After an hour the waterfall was still 5[[1/3]] km away. How far had they hiked?
**Solution**
8[[5/8]] − 5[[1/3]] = 3 + [[15/24]] − [[8/24]] = 3[[7/24]] **km**
## ✏️ Example 3.13
If you add two fractions and the sum is greater than [[1/2]], what can you say about the fractions?
**Solution**
At least one of the fractions must be greater than [[1/4]]. (If both were [[1/4]] or less, their sum would be [[1/2]] or less.) For example [[1/3]] + [[1/5]] = [[8/15]] > [[1/2]], and [[1/3]] > [[1/4]]. Try to find other examples and discuss them with a partner.

6. Explain to a friend why [[1/2]] + [[1/3]] is not [[2/5]].

pages.title: Multiplying fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Explain the process of multiplying a fraction (common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths) by a whole number and by a fraction.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.3.3.1
## Whole number × fraction ("times")
3 × 2[[2/3]] means 3 times 2[[2/3]], or 3 groups of 2[[2/3]].
> 🔑 **Key idea: Multiplying fractions** — (i) Change all numbers (mixed and whole) into common fractions; (ii) multiply the numerators together and the denominators together; (iii) simplify the result. Steps (ii) and (iii) may be swapped by cancelling common factors first.
## ✏️ Example 3.14
Find a) 3 × 2[[2/3]] b) 15 × [[2/3]] c) 12 × [[3/8]]
**Solution**
a) 3 × 2[[2/3]] = [[3/1]] × [[8/3]] = [[24/3]] = **8**
b) 15 × [[2/3]] = [[15×2/3]] = [[30/3]] = **10**
c) 12 × [[3/8]] = [[36/8]] = 4[[1/2]]
## Fraction × whole number ("of")
[[2/3]] × 5 means [[2/3]] **of** 5.
## ✏️ Example 3.15
Find a) [[2/3]] × 5 b) [[2/3]] × 240 c) [[3/8]] × 480
**Solution**
a) [[2/3]] × [[5/1]] = [[10/3]] = 3[[1/3]]
b) [[2/3]] × 240 = 2 × 80 = **160**
c) [[3/8]] × 480 = 3 × 60 = **180**
## Percentages of a quantity
## ✏️ Example 3.16
Calculate (round to the nearest tenth where necessary): a) 28% of 40 b) 234% of 8 c) 3[[1/2]]% of 50 d) 0.2% of 15,000 e) 8.25% of 62
**Solution**
a) [[28/100]] × 40 = **11.2**
b) [[234/100]] × 8 = 18.72 ≈ **18.7**
c) 3.5% of 50 = [[3.5/100]] × 50 = 1.75 ≈ **1.8**
d) [[0.2/100]] × 15,000 = **30**
e) [[8.25/100]] × 62 = 5.115 ≈ **5.1**

pages.title: Fraction × fraction
pages.body:
## Fraction × fraction
## ✏️ Example 3.17
Find a) [[2/3]] × [[1/2]] b) [[2/3]] × [[3/5]] c) [[3/8]] × [[5/6]]
**Solution**
a) [[2/3]] × [[1/2]] = [[2×1/3×2]] = [[2/6]] = [[1/3]]
b) [[2/3]] × [[3/5]] = [[6/15]] = [[2/5]]
c) [[3/8]] × [[5/6]] = [[15/48]] = [[5/16]]
[[fig:m7-f13|Figure 3.5: Area model: 2/3 of 1/2 = 2/6 = 1/3]]
## Decimal × whole number and decimal × decimal
Multiply as if the numbers were whole numbers, then place the decimal point so that the answer has as many decimal places as the two factors together.
0.35 × 6 = 2.10 = 2.1 0.4 × 0.07 = 0.028 (1 + 2 = 3 decimal places)
**Indicator B7.1.3.3.2** Find a fraction of a given quantity (money or a quantity of objects).
## ✏️ Example 3.18
a) Find [[2/3]] of GH₵60. b) There are 132 learners in a class. If [[5/12]] of them are girls, how many boys are there?
**Solution**
a) [[2/3]] × [[60/1]] = [[2×60/3]] = **GH₵40**
b) Girls = [[5/12]] × 132 = 5 × 11 = 55. Boys = 132 − 55 = **77**. (Or: boys = [[7/12]] × 132 = 77.)
## ✏️ Example 3.19
The pie chart shows the ages of learners in a Primary 5 class.
[[fig:m7-f14]]
a) What fraction of the learners are 10 years old? b) How many learners are 11 years old if there are 32 learners in the class?
**Solution**
a) The 10-year-old sector is [[3/8]] of the circle.
b) [[5/16]] × 32 = **10 learners**

pages.title: Dividing fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Explain the process of dividing a fraction (common, percent and decimal fractions up to thousandths) by a 1-digit whole number and by a fraction.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.3.3.3
3 ÷ [[1/4]] means "how many quarters are there in 3?" — or "[[1/4]] × what = 3?"
[[fig:m7-f15|Figure 3.6: There are 12 quarters in 3, so 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Reciprocal and division** — The **reciprocal** of [[a/b]] is [[b/a]] (the product of a number and its reciprocal is 1). To divide by a fraction, multiply both the dividend and the divisor by the reciprocal of the divisor; the divisor becomes 1. In short: **dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.**
## ✏️ Example 3.20
Find a) 3 ÷ [[1/4]] b) [[1/4]] ÷ 3
**Solution**
a) The reciprocal of [[1/4]] is [[4/1]]:
3 ÷ [[1/4]] → (3 × [[4/1]]) ÷ ([[1/4]] × [[4/1]]) = 12 ÷ 1 = **12**
b) The reciprocal of 3 is [[1/3]]:
[[1/4]] ÷ 3 → ([[1/4]] × [[1/3]]) ÷ (3 × [[1/3]]) = [[1/12]] ÷ 1 = [[1/12]]
## ✏️ Example 3.21
Divide: a) 5 ÷ 1[[1/4]] b) [[5/8]] ÷ [[1/2]] c) 0.36 ÷ 4 d) [[7/9]] ÷ 7
**Solution**
a) 5 ÷ [[5/4]] = 5 × [[4/5]] = **4**
b) [[5/8]] × [[2/1]] = [[10/8]] = 1[[1/4]]
c) 0.36 ÷ 4 = **0.09**
d) [[7/9]] × [[1/7]] = [[1/9]]
**Indicator B7.1.3.3.4** Determine the result of dividing a quantity (money or objects) or a fraction by a fraction.

pages.title: Example 3.22
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 3.22
A stack of plates for serving snacks at a party weighs 10 kg. If each plate weighs [[1/4]] kg, how many plates are in the stack?
**Solution**
10 ÷ [[1/4]] → (10 × [[4/1]]) ÷ ([[1/4]] × [[4/1]]) = 40 ÷ 1 = **40 plates**
## ✏️ Example 3.23
A class was given 9[[1/2]] litres of fruit juice to share equally. If there are 38 learners, how many millilitres of juice will each learner get?
**Solution**
9[[1/2]] litres = 9,500 ml; 9,500 ÷ 38 = **250 ml** each
Or using fractions: [[19/2]] ÷ 38 = [[19/2]] × [[1/38]] = [[1/4]] litre = 250 ml.
## ✏️ Example 3.24
In the pie chart of Section 3.4, [[3/8]] of the learners are 10 years old. How many learners are in the class if there are twelve 10-year-old learners?
**Solution**
[[3/8]] of the class = 12 learners, so the class = 12 ÷ [[3/8]] = 12 × [[8/3]] = **32 learners**.

pages.title: Chapter 3 summary
pages.body:
- Equivalent fractions: multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the same number.
- Benchmark equivalents: [[1/2]] = 0.5 = 50%, [[1/4]] = 0.25 = 25%, [[1/5]] = 0.2 = 20%, [[1/10]] = 0.1 = 10%, [[1/3]] ≈ 0.333 = 33[[1/3]]%.
- To compare or order, change everything to the same form.
- Add/subtract: use a common denominator. Multiply: numerator × numerator, denominator × denominator. Divide: multiply by the reciprocal.
- "Of" means multiply: [[3/4]] of 20 = [[3/4]] × 20 = 15.

questions.q: Express [[45/60]] in simplest form and as a percentage.
A rope is 20[[1/4]] m long. Pieces of 2[[1/4]] m are cut from it. How many pieces are obtained?
A school has 840 learners. [[3/7]] of them are boys. 25% of the girls are in JHS 1. How many JHS 1 girls are there?
Mansa used [[2/5]] of her money on Monday and [[1/3]] of it on Tuesday. She had GH₵48 left. How much did she have at first?
Kofi says [[3/8]] > 40%. Is he right? Explain.
